title: Machine-learning analysis links glycolysis-related genes to osteosarcoma metastasis and survival
summary: Public osteosarcoma expression cohorts yielded a glycolysis-related survival score, and machine-learning ranking prioritized a metastasis-associated candidate subsequently tested in cell assays. Risk-group associations were checked in two additional GEO cohorts; the clinical evidence is retrospective, and the cell results do not establish patient-level causality.
ai_technology: Random forest and support-vector-machine feature ranking prioritized candidate genes; Cox regression formed the survival score.
organization: Department of Orthopaedics, Dongguan Tungwah Hospital, Dongguan, Guangdong, China

evidence.tested: The study reports a 13-gene survival score evaluated in TARGET and two GEO cohorts; machine-learning ranking guided a cell-based follow-up of a metastasis-associated candidate.
evidence.unknown: The survival associations are retrospective; the cell assay does not establish patient-level causality or clinical utility.
evidence.ai_role: Random forest and support-vector-machine feature ranking prioritized candidate genes; Cox regression formed the survival score.

source_review.scope: Primary full-text review as recorded in case evidence; record-level claim and attribution review.
